injuries.body_part: bladder / neural pathways relating to voiding
source: the Plaintiff developed urine retention. Foley catheterization was given, which was weaned off before his discharge.
urodynamic study performed on 10 March 2004 shown decrease in bladder sensation and straining pattern during voiding.
Video urodynamic study on 26 January 2006 shown normal filling phase and failure in voiding.
Dr. Leong stated it was possible that the Plaintiff had a neuropathic bladder by reason of the injury of the 2nd and 3rd lumbar vertebra.
the Plaintiff also complained of erectile dysfunction and penile pain on erection.
Examination shown presence of nocturnal erection at sleep suggesting that the erectile dysfunction was more functional than physical.

Dr. Koo also believed that the erectile dysfunction was partly psychological (as there was nocturnal erection) and partly neurogenic as suggested by reason of the very weak bulbo cavernosus reflex and its onset following the accident.

manifestations.description: urine retention; Foley catheterisation initially required; decreased bladder sensation and straining pattern on urodynamic study; failure in voiding on video urodynamic study; needs to sit and strain to pass urine; takes long time to pass urine (20 minutes).
erectile dysfunction and penile pain on erection; presence of nocturnal erection noted.
very very weak bulbo cavernosus reflex
muscle wasting of left thigh (girth of thigh: 44 cm (right); 42 cm (left))
limited forward flexion at 20° (normal range is > 60°)

reduced walking and standing tolerance: can walk about 30 m without crutch; can walk continuously for 35-40 minutes with a crutch then needs 10-15 minutes rest; can stand 5 minutes without crutch and 10-15 minutes with crutch; sitting tolerance of 2 hours; difficulty squatting, stooping and climbing steps

treatments_received: Open reduction and internal fixation for the fractured left tibia on 21 August 2003
Out-patient physiotherapy at Yan Chai Hospital from 19 November 2003 to 23 June 2004
Occupational therapy at Yan Chai Hospital between 27 March 2004 and 28 June 2004
Occupational Therapy at PMH from 30 July 2004 to 14 January 2005
Physiotherapy at PMH between 12 July 2004 and 17 January 2005
Screws removed from left foot on 1 March 2004
Removal of metal plate and screws on 12 October 2004

losses.description: Reduced ability to walk and stand for prolonged periods; requires crutch for longer walking; difficulty climbing steps and stooping; muscle wasting of left thigh and limited forward flexion.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
